item.description: In The Melting Pot, Leyad Zavriyev ’27 explores the immigrant-run culinary scene of Rhode Island by interviewing local restaurant owners. This second episode features Mohamed, whose Moroccan café Tea in Sahara has been a beloved staple of the Providence community for over 15 years. item.title: Spray-Painting Politics: From Bed-Stuy to La Boca - Brown Political Review
item.description: In this photo collection, Leyad Zavriyev explores street art and graffiti from neighborhoods across the world – from Buenos Aires and San Juan, to Marrakech and Brooklyn. These walls tell stories of struggle, resilience, memory, and pride: remembering victims of dictatorship, honoring cultural icons, and calling for justice. What unites them is how they turn everyday streets into open-air galleries, […]

item.title: The Inequality of Air Quality in America - Brown Political Review
item.description: Safe air is disproportionately concentrated in more affluent communities, while minorities and low income populations are burdened with higher pollution levels.

item.title: Evicting the Record: Automatically - Brown Political Review
item.description: In Rhode Island, 6,328 households were thrown into the eviction process over the past year. item.title: Imported Morality: How Colonialism Redrew the Sexual Thresholds of the Egypt - Brown Political Review
item.description: Meet Nyankhkhnum and Khnumhotep, two men buried together in the same tomb during the 5th dynasty in Egypt. Despite both having wives and families, the painting shows them embracing and touching noses. In Egyptian art, this act represents a kiss.
